closed_children.title: v0.4 Phase 1: generalize lernie dispatch CLI for arbitrary roles

description:
Milestone per ARCHITECTURE.md §12 v0.4.

Success criterion (quoted): Agent can dispatch a subagent conversation. The subagent runs in its own worktree and branch. Merge-back flow works end-to-end (including the merge=ours discipline on goal.md/soul.md/summary/**, §2.6). Parallel subagent conversations do not corrupt each other's state. Handle-based async works: a dispatch returns immediately with a handle, siblings can be in flight concurrently, and await(handle) retrieves the compacted result on a later step (§2.5).

=== Scope ===

- Two new built-in tools wired into the worker's tool list:
  - dispatch(role, goal): spawns a subagent conversation off the commit where the dispatch tool-call landed on the parent branch (§2.5). Returns immediately with {status: in_progress, handle: <sub-conv-id>} as the tool_result. Tool-call record committed per §3.3 on the parent branch.
  - await(handle): blocks until the named subagent has merged back (or terminated stopped/conflicted). Returns the subagent's terminal-compacted summary (or status object) as tool_result.content.
- Subagent conversation primitive: lernie dispatch worker <repo> <parent-branch> --goal <goal>. Spawns a sibling worktree at <conv-repo>/<parent>-<sub>/, on branch <parent>-<sub> (full hyphenated descent per §2.3). Writes goal.md and soul.md (sourced from souls/<role>.md) on the dispatch commit. Runs the same multi-step loop the root conversation runs, including its own tool calls and (recursively) further dispatches.
- Merge-back generalization: the merge=ours alignment step (§2.6) currently exercised by the compactor is verified to work for arbitrary subagent merge-backs. Subagent goal.md, soul.md, summary/** stay on the subagent branch; subagent steps/<sub-id>/ does cross up.
- Parallel safety: two dispatches from one parent step spawn two sibling subagent branches off the same commit, both run, both merge back without colliding. Per §2.5 the harness assigns write paths so collisions are structural-impossible; v0.4 verifies and tests this.
- Handle-based async at the wire level: §2.5 requires every tool_use in a step to be paired with a tool_result on the next step. dispatch returns the in_progress handle synchronously in that pairing, the agent emits subsequent steps, and an await(handle) on a later step is what blocks on the subagent. Loop continues to advance other tool_use blocks while one is awaited; awaits within a single step are sequential (single-author-per-file).
- Oversized-output auto-dispatch (§3.3 last bullet, §11): tool output exceeding a sizing heuristic is handed to a parsing subagent automatically; only the parsing subagent's compacted output reaches the parent step. §11 names this as v0.4 work.

=== Pinned by spec, not in scope to redecide ===

- Branch naming = full hyphenated descent of conv-ids; no ex/, inv/, sub/ prefixes (§2.3, post-abfe713).
- Worktrees are siblings of root/, never nested (§2.2 — git does not permit nested working trees).
- merge=ours discipline mechanics: alignment step in the harness, .gitattributes as backstop (§2.6 — already implemented for compactor; v0.4 generalizes).
- Tool stdio contract for dispatch/await: same as any other in-process tool (§3.3 stdio contract). Schemas live at <harness-root>/tools/<name>.json; skills at <harness-root>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.

=== Hard dependencies ===

- bl-7c23 (v0.3 layout migration) — Phase 7 still in flight at filing time. v0.4 assumes the new layout end to end (siblings, hyphenated branches, steps/<conv-id>/NNN/, merge=ours active).
- bl-683c (v0.3 tools) — bash still in flight at filing time. The tool executor and tool-result wire shape are reused verbatim for dispatch/await. Block claim of v0.4 phase 2+ until these merge.

=== Phases (claim in order) ===

Each phase is its own ball with its own tests/docs/alignment gates per AGENTS.md. Phase boundaries are chosen so each fits well under the 300-line cap and lands as one bl review. Phases 2 and 3 are tightly coupled (dispatch tool without await is unusable), so the claimer may fold them if natural.

1. Phase 1 — Generalize the dispatch CLI: lernie dispatch worker <repo> <parent-branch> --goal <goal>. Generalize lernie dispatch from the compactor-only shape to handle arbitrary roles. Branch + worktree spawn machinery generalized; existing compactor case unchanged.
2. Phase 2 — Built-in tool: dispatch. Schema, SKILL.md, in-process binary entry. Returns {status: in_progress, handle: <sub-conv-id>}. Spawns the subagent via the Phase 1 CLI but does not block. Tool-call commit on parent branch.
3. Phase 3 — Built-in tool: await. Blocks on the named subagent's terminal merge (or stopped/conflicted state). Returns the compacted summary or status object. Tool-call commit on parent branch.
4. Phase 4 — Subagent loop end-to-end. The dispatched worker subagent runs the same multi-step loop as the root conversation: model call, tool calls, terminal compaction, merge-back to parent. Recursive dispatch supported (subagent dispatching its own subagents, hyphenated descent extends).
5. Phase 5 — Parallel subagent fixture + write-path assignment. Two sibling dispatches from one step. Both run, both merge back. Test that single-author-per-file (§2.5) holds. Verify merge=ours discipline on goal/soul/summary across sibling merges.
6. Phase 6 — Oversized tool-output auto-dispatch (§3.3 last bullet, §11). Sizing heuristic + parsing-subagent handoff. Raw output never reaches the parent step when oversized.
7. Phase 7 — Default worker tools include dispatch + await. Update template/providers.yaml roles.worker.tools list. Verify the surfaced tools list flows through to the model call.

=== Out of scope ===

- check(handle) (non-blocking poll). §2.5 names it alongside await; v0.4 minimal ships only the blocking await. Filed as a follow-on if needed.
- Workflow.yaml event bindings for subagent lifecycle (worker_return, dispatch(verifier), etc). That's v0.6.
- Verifier/adversary roles. v0.6.
- UI rendering of nested subagent trees with arrows. v0.5 (already in flight as bl-c0a5).
- Cross-conversation memory or shared state between sibling subagents (§11 deferred).

=== Done-when ===

End-to-end: a prompt that drives the worker to emit two parallel dispatch tool_use blocks resolves into two sibling subagent branches off the parent's tool-call commit; both subagents run their own multi-step loops; both merge back; await(handle) on each retrieves the compacted summary; the parent step continues and eventually merges to main. cargo test + tarpaulin --fail-under 100 green on merge. All three gates closed.
